summary.text: Rick Crawford is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 1st District, first elected in 2010, and is seeking re-election. An Army veteran and former agricultural broadcaster, he has served on the House Intelligence Committee since 2017 and became its chairman in January 2025. He also sits on the Agriculture and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

paragraphs.text: Raised in an Air Force family, he lived in various parts of the United States and in England, according to his official biography.
Enlisted in the U.S. Army out of high school and served four years as an Explosive Ordnance Disposal Technician, reaching the rank of sergeant (Ballotpedia lists 1985 to 1989).
Earned a degree in agriculture business and economics from Arkansas State University in 1996; competed in rodeos in college and afterward worked as a freelance rodeo announcer and producer.

Worked in agricultural news reporting and broadcasting, founded and operated the AgWatch Network, a web-based farm news provider serving radio stations in five states, and served as marketing manager for a large John Deere dealer group.

Ran for Congress in 2010 and was first elected that year; Talk Business & Politics reports he was the first Republican to hold the seat since Reconstruction and has won every primary and general election since.
Has served on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence since 2017 and became its chairman in January 2025; previously chaired its CIA Subcommittee.
A senior member of the House Agriculture Committee, he served on the farm bill conference committees in 2014 and 2018 and chaired Agriculture subcommittees in three of his first five terms.

Is vice chairman of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and previously chaired its Highways and Transit Subcommittee; his office credits him with the Interstate 555 designation in Northeast Arkansas.
According to his official biography, he lives in Jonesboro with his wife, Stacy, and their two children, and plays guitar and sings in a band called Triple Nickel.
